page: The Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 6 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs, derived from 3 physical cores with hyper-threading running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA. This compute resource is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Local storage is bundled with the instance, providing 320 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. This high-speed storage medium supports local read and write operations directly on the host. For connectivity, the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs or hardware accelerators present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a mixed performance profile. Single-core processing is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1272.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 796.0. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core reaching 6774.42. Memory read bandwidth is average, peaking at 407.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks, though uncached large-block writes drop to a weak 18.72 GB/sec. Text and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, perform poorly. Conversely, Redis SET operations show average throughput at 6.15 million operations per second, and small LLM text generation achieves an average speed of 97.28 tokens per second.

Given the shared CPU allocation and modest single-core performance, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution but do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is well-suited for general-purpose tasks, lightweight web serving, Redis caching layers, and development environments where resource density and local NVMe storage are prioritized over raw compute power.
